decisions.rationale: Separates collection from judgment and prevents missing evidence from becoming success.
acceptance_tests: collector cannot emit verdicts
missing or contradictory evidence is inconclusive or rejected
review manifest is hash-pinned and signed

decisions.rationale: Real-node fixtures catch descriptor, control-block, output and conflict-policy mistakes that pure unit tests miss.
acceptance_tests: fresh wallets per run
descriptor-derived script equals independently derived script
claim and refund conflict probes execute on Bitcoin Core

decisions.rationale: Useful as an independent fallback oracle, but it would regress DOM's scriptless key-path claim privacy and uses CLTV rather than DOM's selected CSV refund profile.
The ideal model usefully enumerates chain, fork, finality, code hash, recipient, amount, outpoint and deadline bindings even though its cryptography is fake.
acceptance_tests: mutation of every instance field changes the authority digest
unknown codec and fork versions fail closed
chain and contract replay vectors are rejected

decisions.rationale: Correctly treats general and signature witness encryption as unresolved research; the ideal implementation is deterministic hashing, not cryptography.

decisions.target: new reveal authority in route-composer plus durable store capability
decisions.rationale: DOM statically orders funding and deadlines, but its EVM claim submission seam does not itself require a fresh all-leg finalized snapshot before publishing the adaptor secret.
acceptance_tests: reorged upstream funding denies reveal
expired or under-budget leg denies reveal
wrong secret point, route, caller or terms denies reveal
RPC error and hostile reverting leg deny without panic
authorization expires and is one-shot

decisions.target: policy calibration tool and signed policy artifact
decisions.rationale: Converts propagation, finality, watcher, censorship and RPC failover observations into explicit action budgets instead of unexplained constants.
acceptance_tests: minimum sample size and schema enforced
outliers and confidence reported
policy digest binds dataset and algorithm version
unsafe zero or negative inputs rejected

decisions.target: route bundle codec and deployment preflight
decisions.rationale: A single committed operator artifact can bind ordering, legs, margins, fees and deployment identities across all services.
acceptance_tests: unknown versions rejected
all chain identities and code hashes bound
deadline graph and fee caps revalidated by every consumer

decisions.target: DOM operational executors and outbox policy
decisions.rationale: Action preflight, mempool acceptance, bounded replacement and fee/bounty caps complement DOM's stronger durable outbox, but Kaystra's monotonic cursor must not be copied.
acceptance_tests: replacement preserves semantic transaction identity
fees cannot exceed committed caps
deep reorg rolls cursor back by block hash
restart replays identical bytes

decisions.rationale: Secret scanning belongs in CI, but the source mutates text in place, misses binary stores and over-redacts public SIDs.
acceptance_tests: canonical evidence is never modified
private keys, mnemonics, nonces and adaptor secrets are detected in text and supported structured stores
public identifiers remain intact
sanitized exports carry a source integrity map

decisions.target: route-composer property tests and model checking
decisions.rationale: The invariants are valuable, but the executable Rust state and adversarial property tests must remain the release gate.
acceptance_tests: randomized multi-leg deadline graphs preserve refund and claim action budgets

decisions.target: route reveal authority and chain executors
decisions.rationale: The executor re-evaluates the current world immediately before lock or redeem and explicitly proves that Unsafe never releases the secret.
acceptance_tests: TOCTOU state change between preparation and broadcast invalidates authorization
unsafe observations never reach secret-bearing broadcaster
decision code has no network or signing side effects

decisions.rationale: Rust/Solidity vectors are useful only after adding chainId, verifyingContract and complete signed ordering semantics.
acceptance_tests: domain replay across chain and contract rejected
arrival timestamp cannot be attacker-mutated
Rust and Solidity digest vectors match

decisions.rationale: Prevents test tooling and embedded keys from accidentally reaching production chains.
acceptance_tests: mainnet and unknown chains rejected before signer creation
preflight sends zero transactions
private keys never appear in debug output

decisions.rationale: Directly tests the highest consequence property: unsafe/reorged state must not publish the cross-leg secret.
acceptance_tests: reorg rollback before claim leaves secret unpublished
counterparty field mutation forces refund or abort
tests use real receipt and block hashes

decisions.rationale: It is a deterministic one-process simulation, not evidence of a 30-node network or real reorg behavior.
Unsigned created_at affects roles and priority, the EIP-712 domain is replayable, storage is volatile, and public hashlock correlation regresses DOM privacy.
DOM currently checks linkage and each header against its self-declared target, but not expected nBits, retarget boundaries or median-time-past from a trusted checkpoint.
acceptance_tests: easy-target forgery rejected
mainnet retarget boundary matches Bitcoin Core
MTP violation rejected
checkpoint context length and compact target validated
header and byte caps enforced before allocation

decisions.rationale: Prevents payment reuse and cross-order ambiguity, but the 31-bit derivation index needs collision handling and on-chain binding must be enforceable rather than informational.
acceptance_tests: every settlement field changes script or authority digest
index collisions retry with committed salt
script derivation independently verified
script cannot be reused across live settlements

decisions.rationale: Permissionless verified extension is useful, but DOM must additionally define canonical-chain or accumulated-work selection and checkpoint governance.
acceptance_tests: forks tracked by accumulated work
checkpoint overwrite impossible
two-step governance and emergency policy tested
deep reorg invalidates dependent reveal capabilities

decisions.target: optional USPE evidence adapter, never the default atomic path
decisions.rationale: Adds a useful low-cost settlement profile for applications that accept challenger-liveness assumptions; it must not weaken adaptor-based atomic settlement.
acceptance_tests: every accepted false claim maps to a concrete on-chain challenge
no single garbage claim blocks an honest claim
no honest claim is challengeable in Rust/Solidity differential vectors
challenger outage is explicit in policy

decisions.rationale: Prices spam, self-challenge and free options, but values must be calibrated from worst-case challenge cost and liveness rather than copied constants.
acceptance_tests: minimum bond exceeds bounded challenge cost
self-challenge is loss-making
parallel claims cannot strand escrow
deposit outcomes cover settle and expiry

decisions.target: DOM EVM contracts handling external assets
decisions.rationale: A hostile receiver cannot wedge settlement and fee-on-transfer behavior cannot silently undercollateralize an order.
acceptance_tests: reverting receiver becomes withdrawable credit
false-return and fee-on-transfer tokens cannot create excess liabilities
reentrancy and accounting invariants hold

decisions.rationale: Cross-implementation agreement at real consensus boundaries is the strongest regression oracle for the portable evidence verifier.
acceptance_tests: Rust, Solidity and Bitcoin Core agree on valid and forged vectors
SegWit txid canonicalization and odd Merkle duplication covered
no-default-features verifier library passes

decisions.rationale: The repository binds a digest and mock verifier interface but contains no production proof system, circuit or audited verifier.

decisions.target: optional challenger service over DOM durable store
decisions.rationale: The explicit fraud/action mapping is useful; the plain append journal must be replaced by DOM's authenticated durable records and canonical reorg handling.
acceptance_tests: every live fraud has an idempotent action
journal records are authenticated and fsynced
reorg rollback cannot suppress a retry
